clue.text: Old copper in standard valve

indicators.note: the first pieces are placed inside the word for standard, as the clue says they go in it

parts.note: stock means standard, as in stock phrases or stock sizes
a copper is a police officer, abbreviated PC for police constable

explanation.surface: A plumber recalls an old copper fitting being part of the standard valve kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests the metal of old pipes, but it is the policeman, PC.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap on a water pipe that shuts off flow is a kind of valve, the main one in a house.

clue.text: Pundit's second childhood, for one

parts.note: childhood is an example of an age of life

explanation.surface: A pundit is accused of being in a second childhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second childhood' reads as dotage, which is no help: 'second' gives S and 'childhood, for one' is an age.
explanation.definitionFit: A wise and learned person, an authority whose opinions are sought, is a sage.

clue.text: Grass is needed by horse, I swear it?

parts.note: oats are a cereal grass
H is slang for heroin, itself slang horse

explanation.surface: Someone swears a horse needs grass, as if anyone doubted it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' is slang for heroin, written H.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'I swear' is the start of a solemn promise or vow, which is what this is.

clue.text: .Rise briefly over ocean, leaving river and coming to a high point

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second
said briefly, a word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to climb is to rise

indicators.note: the river abbreviation leaves the ocean's name, so it is taken out

parts.note: the Arctic is an ocean

explanation.surface: A climb rises over the ocean, leaves a river behind and reaches a summit.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something forming the peak or culmination of a build-up.

clue.text: Brown and black farm animal, sweetly pretty

parts.note: chocolate is a shade of brown
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an ox is a farm animal

explanation.surface: A brown and black farm animal is called sweetly pretty.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes chocolate-box lids' twee pictures, so anything prettily conventional.

clue.text: Rigorous limit avoid by engineers

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep away from it, so these letters are left out of the longer word

parts.note: to restrict is to limit
RE stands for Royal Engineers, the British Army corps

explanation.surface: A demand that a strict limit be kept, avoided only by engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove RE (Royal Engineers, a British Army corps) from RESTRICT.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe rules applied exactly and severely with no leniency.

clue.text: One to be taken by the force?

definitions.text: One to be taken by the force?

parts.words: One to be taken by the force?
parts.note: a criminal the police force will arrest, who also takes things by force

explanation.surface: A question about who the police should arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The force' is the police, who take a robber into custody; read the other way, a robber takes things by force.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who steals is the kind of person the police are out to arrest.

clue.text: Better to conceal one's made up

indicators.note: concealing something hides it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to better is to improve, and improved means made better
I for one, plus 's as is

explanation.surface: Someone says it is better to hide that they invented a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is I (one) plus IS, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made up on the spot, invented without preparation, is ad-libbed.

clue.text: With drink man would take food at hotel without ever letting up

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits
he is a man
to eat is to take food
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man with a drink would carry on eating at the hotel relentlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight that continues until one side is killed never slackens, hence relentless.

clue.text: I'd forget to recycle sack

indicators.note: recycling turns material into something new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admits forgetting to put the sack out for recycling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like a bag of recycling, but it is the verb meaning dismiss.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack an employee is to dismiss them, which is to remove them from the job.

clue.text: Stole what diner may leave with dog?

parts.note: a diner may leave a tip for the waiter
a dog is a typical pet

explanation.surface: A question about what a diner who left with a dog might have taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' reads as the past tense of steal, but it is the noun: a scarf or wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A short cape or scarf worn over the shoulders, a fur wrap, is a type of stole.

clue.text: Teach recruit badly, it's a fine art

indicators.note: done badly, the letters come out in a muddled order

explanation.surface: Teaching a recruit poorly is said to be a fine art.
explanation.definitionFit: Building design is traditionally ranked among the fine arts alongside painting and sculpture.

clue.text: Will's lost unpaid work

definitions.meaning: Will Shakespeare's comedy Love's Labour's Lost: in the title the lover's toil is what is lost
a task done for the pleasure of it, without payment

explanation.surface: Someone laments that a man named Will has lost his unpaid work.
explanation.walkthrough: Will is Shakespeare; his play Love's Labour's Lost puts the phrase, in another order, in its title.
explanation.definitionFit: Work undertaken willingly for its own sake rather than for pay is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Put down sums for models

parts.note: to lay is to put down
figures are sums or numbers

explanation.surface: An instruction to write down the totals for some models.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists' jointed wooden mannequins used for posing drapery are models of the human form.

clue.text: Full of noise, harangue in support of county match

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath the other
one word is full of the other, holding it inside

parts.note: to orate is to harangue, speaking pompously
din is noise

explanation.surface: A noisy rant in support of a county cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' is the verb, to make things go together, not a game.
explanation.definitionFit: To make things harmonise, such as clothes and colours, is to bring them into agreement.

clue.text: Take notice? No point

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a notice
O is nought, zero, so none

explanation.surface: Someone told to take notice replies that there is no point.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on a child, a name or a policy as one's own is to embrace it in this sense.

clue.text: One hard poet translated is Paris prizewinner

indicators.note: a translation turns words into new forms, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A difficult poet, once translated, wins a prize in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris' suggests the French capital, but it is the Trojan prince who judged the beauty contest among three goddesses and gave the golden apple to the goddess of love.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the goddess of love won the golden apple when Paris judged her the fairest.

clue.text: Deliberately forward contract, work being held up

parts.note: on means forward, as in moving on

indicators.note: the outer word holds the reversed piece inside it

parts.note: to purse the lips is to contract them

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A forward contract deliberately held up while work continues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a legal agreement, but it is the verb, as in pursing the lips.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something intentionally rather than by accident is acting with design.

clue.text: Unlimited confidence in primordial bird

indicators.note: the trimmed word is placed inside the word for primordial, as the clue says it goes in it

parts.note: primordial means existing at the very beginning, first

indicators.note: without limits, the outer letters at each end are dropped

parts.note: a confidence is a secret shared

explanation.surface: A claim that unlimited confidence lies within some primordial bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confidence' looks like self-assurance, but here it is a secret told in confidence; 'Unlimited' strips its outer letters to leave ECRE.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny European songbird with a flame-coloured crown stripe is a close relative of the goldcrest.

clue.text: Gather urgent request needs time

parts.note: a plea is an urgent appeal

explanation.surface: Instructions to gather because an urgent request needs time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gather' looks like assemble, but it is the dressmaker's word for a fold in cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: In sewing, a gather is a fold drawn into fabric, much like a crease pressed into a skirt.

clue.text: Profitable business's general condition leading to worry

parts.note: the going is the state of things, as in the going at a racecourse
concern means worry

explanation.surface: A firm's general state is giving rise to worry.
explanation.definitionFit: Accountants use the phrase for a firm trading viably and expected to continue, so a sound enterprise.

clue.text: Gold edging for English jacket

indicators.note: the gold word edges, surrounding the other letter on both sides

parts.note: gilt is gold leaf or gold-coloured

explanation.surface: A gold trim made for an English jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless padded garment worn over a shirt is a type of jacket or waistcoat.

clue.text: Tropical plant not fully bedded down

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, so the letters lie within it

explanation.surface: A tropical plant has not been fully bedded into the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: This edible tuber, also called taro, is grown across the tropics, a starchy plant.

clue.text: Liberal, like some public houses

definitions.meaning: a British ... house is a pub not tied to one brewery

explanation.surface: Some pubs are described as liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: A liberal person is unrestrained and open-handed; a pub not tied to one brewer is likewise unrestricted.

clue.text: A pound in the bank; are you sure?

indicators.note: the first pieces sit inside the word for bank, as the clue puts them in it

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it
L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for a pound

explanation.surface: Someone doubts that there is a pound in their bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is the verb, as in banking on something, giving RELY.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of surprise or doubt asking whether something is true, like 'is that so?'

clue.text: A number of families from America turned back at the frontier

indicators.note: turning back reverses the direction, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: US is short for the United States of America
a frontier is a border between countries

explanation.surface: Several families from America were turned back at the border.
explanation.walkthrough: In biological classification a level between order and family groups several families.
explanation.definitionFit: A biological rank below an order and above the family, so it holds several families.

clue.text: Shelter in squalid place, from such weather?

definitions.note: the clue's noun phrase stands for an adjective describing that kind of weather

indicators.note: the shelter word is placed inside the word for a squalid place

parts.note: a sty is a pigpen, a filthy place
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: Seeking shelter in a squalid hovel to escape such bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes wet, icy weather where rain and snow fall half-frozen.

clue.text: Woman and writer go off to marry

parts.note: a pen is something to write with
to elope is to run away to marry secretly

explanation.surface: A woman and an author run off together to wed.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, borne by Odysseus's faithful wife in Homer, so an example of a woman.
